## 1. Prerequisites & Skill Assessment

### Basic R Programming Skills Required

You should be comfortable with:

- R syntax (objects, functions, operators)
- Basic data structures: vectors, factors, data frames, and lists
- Indexing and subsetting data
- Writing simple R scripts
- Reading and importing data (`read.csv()`, `read.table()`, or `readr`)

### Assess Your Skills

If you're unsure, evaluate your R knowledge with one of these:

- [Google Form Assessment](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdIyeuabd_ZOWXgI1MWHapmaOMu20L9ESkLDZiWnpmkpujyOg/viewform)
- [Coursera R Programming Skill Assessment](https://www.coursera.org/resources/r-programming-skill-assessment)
- [NCEAS R Review and Assessment](https://nceas.github.io/oss-lessons/r-review-and-assessment/r-review-and-assessment.html)

::: {.callout-warning}
**Still unsure?** Email [deepak.tanwar@uzh.ch](mailto:deepak.tanwar@uzh.ch) before the course to discuss whether this workshop is a good fit.
:::

## 2. Install R (Version 4.6.2)

::: {.panel-tabset}

### macOS

**Using Homebrew (recommended):**

1. If you don't have Homebrew installed, install it first:
   ```bash
   /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
   ```

2. Install R:
   ```bash
   brew install r
   ```

**Or download directly:**

1. Go to [CRAN - R for macOS](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/)
2. Download **R-4.6.2-arm64.pkg** (Apple Silicon) or **R-4.6.2-x86_64.pkg** (Intel)
3. Open the `.pkg` file and follow the installer

**Verify installation:**

```bash
R --version
```

### Windows

1. Go to [CRAN - R for Windows](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/)
2. Click **Download R 4.6.2 for Windows**
3. Open the `.exe` file and follow the installer
4. Use all default options

**Verify installation:**

Open **Command Prompt** or **PowerShell** and run:

```cmd
R --version
```

### Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

Add the CRAN repository and install:

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y dirmngr gnupg apt-transport-https ca-certificates software-properties-common
sudo add-apt-repository "deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu $(lsb_release -cs)-cran40/"
sudo apt-key adv --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys E298A3A825C0D65DFD57CBB651716619E084DAB9
sudo apt install -y r-base r-base-dev
```

**Verify installation:**

```bash
R --version
```

:::

---

## 3. Install RStudio

RStudio is the integrated development environment (IDE) you'll use for this course.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### macOS

1. Go to [RStudio Download](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
2. Click **Download for macOS**
3. Open the `.dmg` file
4. Drag RStudio into the **Applications** folder
5. Launch RStudio from Applications

### Windows

1. Go to [RStudio Download](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
2. Click **Download for Windows**
3. Open the `.exe` file
4. Follow the installer with default options
5. Launch RStudio from the Start menu

### Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)

**Using your package manager (recommended — always gets latest):**

```bash
sudo apt install -y rstudio
```

**Or download the latest version directly:**

1. Go to [RStudio Download](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
2. Choose **Linux** and your distribution
3. Download the `.deb` file
4. Install:
   ```bash
   sudo dpkg -i rstudio-*.deb
   sudo apt install -f  # Fix any missing dependencies
   ```

Launch RStudio:

```bash
rstudio &
```

:::

**Verify installation:**

Open RStudio. In the **Console** (bottom left), run:

```r
R.version$version.string
```

You should see version 4.6.2 or later.

---

## 4. Install renv for Reproducible Environments

**renv** ensures all participants use the same R package versions. Install it first:

```r
install.packages("renv")
```

Verify:

```r
library(renv)
renv::version()
```

---

## 5. Set Up the Course Repository

### Step 1 — Clone the repository

::: {.panel-tabset}

### macOS / Linux

Open **Terminal** and run:

```bash
cd ~/Documents
git clone https://github.com/DQBM-CCCZ/publication_ready_figs_R.git
cd publication_ready_figs_R
```

### Windows

Open **Command Prompt** or **PowerShell** and run:

```cmd
cd %USERPROFILE%\Documents
git clone https://github.com/DQBM-CCCZ/publication_ready_figs_R.git
cd publication_ready_figs_R
```

:::

### Step 2 — Restore packages using renv.lock

In RStudio, open the project: **File → Open Project... → publication_ready_figs_R.Rproj**

Then in the **Console**, run:

```r
renv::restore("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DQBM-CCCZ/publication_ready_figs_R/refs/heads/main/renv.lock")
```

This downloads and installs all packages in the exact versions specified. It may take 10–15 minutes on first run.

**Expected output:**

```
✓ All done!
# [1] "All done!"
```

Before the course day, run all these checks:

::: {.panel-tabset}

```

### Windows (Command Prompt)

# Check git

# Launch RStudio

```

### RStudio Console (all platforms)

```r

renv::status()

# Check key packages are installed
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(tidyverse)
```

:::

**All checks should pass with no errors.**

## Troubleshooting

### R or RStudio won't install?

Check your OS has sufficient disk space (at least 500 MB). If you get permission errors on Linux, use `sudo` or ask your system administrator.

### Git is not recognized?

You may need to restart your Terminal/Command Prompt after installing Git.

### renv::restore() fails?

1. Update your packages:
   ```r
   update.packages()
   ```
2. Try again:
   ```r
   renv::restore()
   ```
3. If still stuck, email [deepak.tanwar@uzh.ch](mailto:deepak.tanwar@uzh.ch) with the error message.

### "Cannot find R" error in RStudio?

Restart RStudio after installing R. If the problem persists, go to **Tools → Global Options → R (General)** and manually set the R version path.
